title: A headless run is told to work in the foreground and never end its turn to wait
name: run-foreground
description: host-avail-7f0g's first run was lost: the agent started the test suite with run_in_background, said it would wait for the notification, called ScheduleWakeup and ended its turn. Under `claude -p` (and `codex exec`) the end of the turn is the end of the process, so nothing was committed and the review saw an empty branch. The closing instructions every brief carries — `HOW_IT_ENDS` in packages/core/src/dispatch.ts (~line 453) — say to commit but not how the session ends. Add one short paragraph there: this is a headless run with nobody to wake it; run every command in the foreground and wait for it; never background a command, schedule a wakeup or wait for a notification; the turn you end is the run you end. Keep it host-neutral (the same text reaches Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and the openrouter loop). Test in packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts that the rendered prompt carries the sentence.

brief.approach:
One paragraph of prompt text and one test.

1. `packages/core/src/dispatch.ts`, `HOW_IT_ENDS` (~line 453): before "Commit your work on this branch.", add a paragraph, host-neutral since the same text reaches Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor and the openrouter loop:

   > This is a headless run and nobody is watching it. The turn you end is the run you end: when you stop, the process exits, and nothing that was still running reports back. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it to finish — never background a command, schedule a wakeup, or stop to wait for a notification. Long commands (the full test suite, coverage) are part of the work; wait for them.

   Extend the doc comment above `HOW_IT_ENDS` with one line naming why: host-avail-7f0g's first run backgrounded its test suite, ended its turn to wait, and the run ended uncommitted.

2. `packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts`: nothing asserts on the prompt today. Add one test that dispatches through the fake host the file already uses and checks the prompt the host received contains `Run every command in the foreground` and still contains `Commit your work on this branch` after it — so the order is kept and the M1-gate sentence is not lost. If the fake host does not expose its argv, export nothing new: read the prompt from the run's recorded input the way the existing tests read other run output.

Nothing else: no host-specific flags, no change to adapters.

acceptance.run: rg -q 'Run every command in the foreground' packages/core/src/dispatch.ts && rg -q 'The turn you end is the run you end' packages/core/src/dispatch.ts
acceptance.proves: The closing instructions every run receives carry the foreground rule

acceptance.run: rg -q 'Run every command in the foreground' packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts && pnpm vitest run packages/core/src/dispatch.test.ts
acceptance.proves: A test reads the prompt a host actually received and finds the rule before the commit instruction

acceptance.run: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test
